title: Telemetry‑led shadow evacuation and rollback priority scorer
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduce telemetry‑driven shadow evacuation with a rollback priority scorer. Adds new scorer service, integrates with rollout conductor, and enables automatic evacuation of shadow and canary lanes when multi‑metric risk crosses thresholds. Backward compatible; opt‑in via rollout config. Includes perf and safety tests.
description: Context: Several incidents during high‑load experiments revealed slow observations of semantic drift and asymmetric latency spikes in shadow lanes, delaying safe evacuation. This PR introduces a telemetry‑led Shadow Evacuation and Rollback Priority Scorer that computes a runtime risk score for lanes (shadow, canary, A/B variants) and surfaces prioritized evacuation actions to the rollout conductor. Motivation: Reduce mean time to safe evacuation, prioritize rollback actions deterministically, and make evacuation decisions explainable to oncall and SREs. What this changes: Adds a new microservice rollout/scorer that ingests aggregated telemetry (latency histograms, 5xx rates, token loss regression signal, embedding drift score, cost delta) and computes a normalized risk score; extends the rollout conductor with a Scorer API client and an evacuation planner; introduces rollout policy fields (evacuation_threshold, priority_weighting, cool_down_window) and an emergency_evacuate action; updates the shadow router to mark lanes as 'evacuation_pending' for controlled drain; introduces a lightweight explainability payload attached to evacuation actions for audit/troubleshooting. Migration and compatibility: Default behavior is no‑op; operators opt in by enabling the scorer in rollout config (example provided in docs). Existing rollout semantics remain unchanged if scorer disabled. Testing: Unit tests for scoring logic and ranking; integration tests that run local simulator with synthetic telemetry; e2e smoke that validates evacuation from shadow lanes and canary lanes under threshold breaches; backfilled synthetic incidents for regression tests. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4821; - [x] Unit tests added and passing; - [x] Integration tests added in perf‑harness; - [x] Docs updated (runbook + conductor API); - [x] Can be toggled via rollout flags for staged enablement; - [x] Load and latency benchmarks validated on benchmark lab. Risks and mitigations: Risk of over‑eager evacuation leading to unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by a cool_down_window and multi‑metric dampening; risk of scorer becoming a single point of failure — scorer client falls back to conservative scoring (no evacuation) on unreachable. Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag, enable in staging for 2 weeks with synthetic shadow trials, ramp to Canary orgs then production. Related: References ENG‑4821 design and SUP‑7332 incident RCA. Commits summary: Commit 1: scaffolding for rollout/scorer service and protobufs; Commit 2: scoring algorithm implementation with multi‑metric normalization and priority ranking; Commit 3: rollout conductor client and evacuation planner; Commit 4: shadow router drain marker and audit payload; Commit 5: integration tests and docs. CI and checks: GitHub Actions matrix for unit/integration; perf lab smoke; static linters; one flaky TestShadowDrainTiming was rerun and passed. Merge: squash merge to main after approvals and green CI.
